Overview

Medellín as a Business Centre

Medellín is Colombia's second city and the capital of Antioquia. The municipality puts its population at about 2.70 million in 2024, using DANE projections based on the 2018 census, and it sits at the centre of the ten-municipality Aburrá Valley. City figures show Medellín generated about 54 percent of Antioquia's GDP in 2023, led by commerce, professional and administrative services, manufacturing, real estate, financial services and construction. Several of Colombia's largest listed groups are associated with the city, including Bancolombia, Grupo SURA, Grupo Argos, Grupo Nutresa, ISA and Celsia. The city's investment agency promotes technology services, business process outsourcing, life sciences, logistics, agribusiness and creative industries, and José María Córdova airport in nearby Rionegro carries international routes.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Medellín because the city combines sophisticated corporate groups with long-standing exposure to illicit finance. Foreign investors and acquirers want to understand Antioquian partners, family holdings and related companies before committing capital. Gold and mineral buyers face particular scrutiny: in February 2025 local media reported the conviction of fifteen people over a scheme run from Medellín that laundered about 2.3 trillion pesos through gold from illegal mining, using shell companies and fictitious exports. Real estate, outsourcing contracts and fast-growing new businesses also generate disputes and integrity questions. Counsel need sourced facts on companies, individuals and assets that may be subject to forfeiture claims.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Medellín

01

Gold and mineral supply chain diligence

Research on gold traders, comercializadoras and their suppliers in Antioquia before purchase or financing, testing whether sellers exist, how long companies have operated, who controls them and whether they appear in prosecutions or forfeiture cases, given documented schemes using shell companies and fictitious exports.

02

Corporate group and partner background

Background research on Antioquian companies, family holding structures and principals ahead of joint ventures, acquisitions or distribution agreements, drawing on chamber of commerce certificates, court records and Spanish-language media, so investors understand ownership, related parties and reputational history.

03

Real estate and asset tracing

Assembling public-record information on property and companies linked to a debtor or counterparty in Medellín and surrounding municipalities, and checking whether assets are already subject to asset forfeiture proceedings, which can affect whether an investor or creditor can rely on them.

04

Outsourcing and services vendor vetting

Due diligence on business process outsourcing, technology and contact centre providers in Medellín before contracts are signed, covering corporate registration, legal representatives, litigation, labour disputes in public records and any links between vendor owners and client employees.

05

Internal fraud and procurement reviews

Support to internal investigations at subsidiaries and operations in Antioquia where kickbacks, inflated invoicing or undisclosed conflicts are suspected, through lawful research into suppliers, their owners and their connections, working with Colombian counsel on evidence handling.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Medellín

Asset forfeiture courts in Medellín

Medellín is a seat of Colombia's specialised asset forfeiture (extinción de dominio) system. The Tribunal Superior de Medellín has a Sala Especializada de Extinción de Dominio, and specialised first-instance forfeiture courts sit in the city; a Medellín forfeiture court took up a claim filed by a Bogotá forfeiture prosecutor in March 2025. Checking whether property or companies are subject to these proceedings is a routine step in Antioquian asset and counterparty research.

Chamber of commerce registry

Companies domiciled in Medellín register with the Cámara de Comercio de Medellín para Antioquia, which keeps the commercial registry for its jurisdiction and issues certificates of existence and legal representation. These certificates identify legal representatives, directors and registered acts, but not necessarily ultimate owners. Shareholdings in sociedades por acciones simplificadas are often not visible in the registry, so ownership questions usually need further documentary work through counsel.

Prosecutions and illicit finance

The Fiscalía General de la Nación investigates money laundering and pursues forfeiture of assets in Antioquia. A ten-year investigation into gold trading from illegal mining between 2001 and 2011 led in 2025 to sentences for fifteen businesspeople and accountants and to the seizure for forfeiture of more than 23 properties in Medellín, Rionegro and other parts of Antioquia. Public reporting of such cases is a useful screening source.

Arbitration and dispute resolution

Commercial contracts with Antioquian parties frequently provide for arbitration in Medellín, commonly administered by the arbitration and conciliation centre of the Cámara de Comercio de Medellín para Antioquia. Investigative support in arbitration is limited to factual research for counsel, presented so that it can be relied on and tested. Confidentiality obligations of the proceeding are respected, and legal strategy remains with Colombian counsel.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Medellín

For matters touching Medellín, TDSC begins by identifying the decision the client faces, whether a partnership, a mineral purchase, a credit exposure or an internal concern, and the Colombian records that bear on it. Research is conducted from Nashville using chamber of commerce certificates, published court decisions, forfeiture and prosecution reporting, and Spanish-language open sources. Because forfeiture risk can attach to property and companies in Antioquia, screening for extinción de dominio proceedings is built into asset and counterparty work. Where interviews, site visits or document collection in Colombia are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified local professionals and the client's Colombian counsel, and personal data is handled under Colombia's data protection rules.

TDSC has no office in Medellín. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Medellín: Frequently Asked Questions

Can you check whether a Medellín property is subject to forfeiture proceedings?

We research published court decisions, notices and media reporting for indications that property or companies are linked to extinción de dominio proceedings, which in Antioquia are heard by specialised courts in Medellín. Formal confirmation from property records and the court file is obtained by Colombian counsel. We report what was found and what could not be confirmed.

How do you vet a gold supplier based in Antioquia?

We look at the supplier's registration history, legal representatives and directors, related companies, any connection to prosecutions or forfeiture cases, and media coverage of the people behind it. Documented schemes have relied on shell sellers and invented exports, so we test whether the business has real operating history. Mining title and traceability checks sit with specialists and counsel.

Does a chamber of commerce certificate show who owns a company?

It shows the company's existence, legal representatives, directors and registered acts. It frequently does not show shareholders, particularly in simplified stock companies. We combine the certificate with filings, court records and open sources to build a picture of control, and identify where counsel needs to request shareholder registers or other documents.

Can you support an arbitration seated in Medellín?

Yes, on factual matters. We research parties, witnesses' corporate roles, related entities and assets for counsel, and present findings with sources so they can be tested. We do not provide legal advice or act as party representatives. Confidentiality obligations of the arbitration apply to everything we receive and produce.

Does TDSC have an office in Medellín?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Medellín or elsewhere in Colombia. Engagements touching the city are scoped and managed from Nashville, with qualified Colombian professionals and the client's local counsel engaged where field work or legal advice is required.
